reason: The developing red cells have protein-making machinery, and haemoglobin is the oxygen-carrying component they need.
expectation: The cells should use the materials to make haemoglobin.

effect: The developing cells made haemoglobin and matured into red blood cells; I can now add oxygen to test their carrying role.
reaction: The maturation picture made the change clear.
reason: Red blood cells contain the haemoglobin needed to carry oxygen.
expectation: The red blood cells should pick up oxygen.

effect: The red cells now carry oxygen, and the result explains how haemoglobin can release it in working tissues. I still need to assemble the surrounding blood sample.
reaction: The reversible binding makes the carrying role clearer.
reason: Plasma water and solutes are the visible components of the liquid part of blood.

reason: The oxygen-bearing red cells belong in the plasma to form a blood sample.
expectation: The red cells should be suspended in the plasma.

effect: Plasma had to receive white cells and platelets before the oxygen-bearing red cells could be added. The compatibility feedback completed that step automatically.
reaction: The required order was surprising; the feedback made the next step clear.
reason: Adding the oxygen-bearing red cells should complete the blood sample.

choice.combine: Plasma with white cells and platelets

expectation: The red cells should join the other blood components in plasma.

effect: The red cells joined the plasma and other components, completing the blood sample and the chapter goal.
reaction: The final picture brings the components together clearly.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding oxygen to the red cells was most worthwhile: the result explained both binding and release, connecting blood to the needs of working tissues.

leastWorthwhile.text: Combining water with solutes was predictable and added little explanation of what the dissolved materials do.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the plasma had to receive white cells and platelets before the red cells. The compatibility feedback handled that step automatically.

arbitrary.text: The required order for adding blood components felt arbitrary because the supplied descriptions did not explain why it mattered.

continue.text: I would choose to continue for another chapter to see how circulation connects the blood to the arm's cells. This chapter made oxygen transport understandable, though most combinations were predictable.
